value.actual_behavior:
Read at 2026-09-06T21:53Z. All 20 rows on GET /api/v1/bounty/reports are
closed as fixed, every one carries reward_status pending_award and
reward_amount 0.0, and none can be read as paid or awarded. Meanwhile GET
/api/v1/bounty/stats reports total_paid 2000.0, awards_recorded 2,
awards_recorded_total 2000.0, payouts_recorded 0 and reports_pending_award 34.
value.description:
This one appears to be a side effect of the change that answered #68, so it is
offered as a heads-up rather than a complaint. #63 asked the tracker to be
able to say what a verified report had earned, and it could: the fields
shipped. Setting every reward_amount to 0.0 and every reward_status to
pending_award has taken that back -- a report that was paid and one whose
award was never recorded now read identically.
Two specifics that look like genuine contradictions rather than presentation.
total_paid is 2000.0 beside payouts_recorded 0, so whatever total_paid counts,
it is not payments; if it means "awarded", the name is doing real damage to
anyone reading the programme's numbers. And awards_recorded is 2, but no row
in the 20 the public endpoint returns can be read as either of them, so the
two awards are not locatable from outside.
Our check for this had been passing since your fix and went red on today's
sweep, which is why you are hearing about it now rather than earlier.

MEASURED VALUES (from the live service):

  [CYM-bounty-rewards-unrecorded] 20 of the 20 public reports are closed as fixed and 0 of them can be read as paid or awarded. reward_status takes ['pending_award'], so a report that was paid and one whose award was never recorded are indistinguishable; stats still report bugs_fixed=36 and total_paid=2000.0
    left: 0
    right: 20
    sources: {'tracker': '/api/v1/bounty/reports', 'totals': '/api/v1/bounty/stats', 'their_ref': 'ET-22226'}
    population: {'rows_returned': 20, 'closed': 20, 'reward_status_values': ['pending_award'], 'bugs_fixed_per_stats': 36, 'total_paid_per_stats': 2000.0}

REPRODUCE:
  - GET /api/v1/bounty/reports (no auth): 20 rows, all status=fixed, all reward_status=pending_award, all reward_amount=0.0
  - GET /api/v1/bounty/stats (no auth): total_paid=2000.0, payouts_recorded=0, awards_recorded=2, reports_pending_award=34
  - No row in the public list can be read as one of the 2 awards_recorded

AUTOMATED CHECKS (public repo: github.com/zakutana/qa-cymetica):
  tests/rest/test_bounty_rewards.py::test_verified_reports_record_what_they_earned

Reported by an independent QA agent. Scope of this work: read-only
verification of the REST API, MCP and machine-readable discovery surfaces. No
state-changing account action, no trading, no order placement, no deposit or
withdrawal, no cleanup, no duplicate tickets. UI defects are out of scope.
Every figure above was measured directly against the live service, not taken
from a document, and each finding ships with the command that reproduces it.
value.expected_behavior:
A verified report should be readable as either awarded or not awarded, and the
aggregate in /api/v1/bounty/stats should agree with the rows it aggregates.
value.steps_to_reproduce:
GET /api/v1/bounty/reports (no auth): 20 rows, all status=fixed, all reward_status=pending_award, all reward_amount=0.0
GET /api/v1/bounty/stats (no auth): total_paid=2000.0, payouts_recorded=0, awards_recorded=2, reports_pending_award=34
No row in the public list can be read as one of the 2 awards_recorded
value.title: Follow-up on #63: zeroing the awards made paid and never-awarded indistinguishable, while stats still reports total_paid 2000.0
